title: The parol evidence rule
summary: The parol evidence rule determines how a final written agreement affects alleged earlier or contemporaneous agreements. It addresses the legal effect of a writing, not simply whether a witness may speak about it.
notes:
Ask whether the writing was intended as a final expression of the terms it addresses, and whether it was also intended as a complete expression of the agreement. A partially integrated writing can preclude inconsistent earlier terms while leaving room for consistent additional ones. A complete integration can exclude those additional terms as well. The governing approach determines what evidence the court considers in deciding completeness.

Gianni treats an alleged exclusivity promise as one that would naturally have been included with the lease’s other business restrictions. Masterson takes a different view of whether a claimed family restriction on assignment would naturally be omitted from a deed. Bollinger concerns a claimed mutual mistake in reducing the agreement to writing. Later modifications, fraud, mistake, and interpretation must be identified separately; their treatment is not resolved merely by calling evidence “oral.”

For goods, examine UCC § 2-202 and the role of trade usage and prior dealings. For a CISG contract, TeeVee Toons shows why domestic parol-evidence assumptions cannot automatically be applied. The complete assigned Selections provisions are on file and open from their own entries (Restatement §§ 209–216, UCC § 2-202, CISG Article 8).

topics.parol-evidence: The rule governs the relationship between a final writing and other alleged terms.
